User request: No tools are available. In this JavaScript snippet, what does `source` mean? `const source = items.filter(Boolean);`

content.text:
`source` is just a variable name. The expression assigns to it a new array containing only the "truthy" elements from `items`.

Explanation: `items.filter(Boolean)` calls `Array.prototype.filter` with `Boolean` as the predicate (equivalent to `x => Boolean(x)`), so any falsy values (false, 0, "", null, undefined, NaN) are removed. `filter` returns a new array; the original `items` is not mutated. If `items` is not an array, `items.filter` will throw.
